| [THEORY-023](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-023.md) v4 | Evidence cannot settle AI consciousness | Birch (2025), [LIT-111](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-111.md): behavioural markers are "gamed", and architectural markers are "Janus-faced", giving a two-level deadlock. | [THEORY-024](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-024.md) v2 | Global sections restore classical Boolean logic | Ghose (2025), [LIT-276](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-276.md) — asserts that the Heyting algebra of truth values "becomes Boolean" when the presheaf data collapse to a global section, and that sheaves encode Boolean reasoning. Both claims are asserted, not proved. The record's readings refute them. The internal logic of a topos is fixed by the base category and its topology, not by whether one presheaf has a section (Isham–Butterfield, [LIT-325](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-325.md), §6). Sheaf toposes such as Sh(ℝ) are not Boolean ([NOTE-249](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-249.md)). The contextuality criterion itself is untouched. | Rejected |
| [THEORY-030](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-030.md) v4 | Landauer prices only losing distinguishability | Bennett (2003), [LIT-360](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-360.md): the cost attaches to many-to-one maps of the logical state, at least k ln 2 of entropy per bit exported to non-information-bearing degrees of freedom, which "need not" be heat. The record derives it for a memory and environment evolving reversibly from an uncorrelated start: the environment's entropy rises by at least the logical entropy lost, H(X \| f(X)), and an injective step has no floor, attained exactly by a permutation. Goldt & Seifert ([LIT-308](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-308.md)) bound information learnt by total entropy production, payable with vanishing heat in their toy model. It does not license a k_BT ln 2 heat floor per judgment, per gradient step or per bit learnt. Whether the bound survives without reversible dynamics is [QUESTION-215](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-215.md). | Active |

| [THEORY-048](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-048.md) | Biology implements psychological functions | Kendler (2008), [LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md): following Marr, a lower-level theory either replaces a higher-level construct (temperature by mean kinetic energy) or implements it, and in psychiatry biology "will implement but not replace psychology". The thesis is argued from neuroscience's successes in perception, learning and memory, not from a psychiatric case, so it is Proposed. It is a thesis about explanation, not about distinct mental causes: it survives Pernu's argument ([LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)) that the neural evidence supports only mental causation by identity. Kendler 2005 ([LIT-552](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-552.md)), which argued the mind–brain propositions this paper develops, is unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-053](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-053.md) | Efficacy is not evidence for a theory of change | Salkovskis, Sighvatsson and Sigurdsson ([LIT-538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)): "The effectiveness of a treatment is not evidence for the validity of the theory on which it is based", with one exception, that changing the theory's crucial factor without changing the problem disconfirms it. Hofmann and Hayes ([LIT-544](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-544.md)), from the other wing of CBT: a model whose process cannot be shown to apply "is incorrect and needs to be set aside" even if the intervention works, and a procedure that fails to move the process leaves the model untested. Active because it is close to a logical point and both state it. What it does not say is that mediation proves a mechanism; both sources deny that. | Active |
| [THEORY-057](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-057.md) | Emotion categories are not natural kinds | Barrett (2017), [LIT-542](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-542.md): degeneracy, population thinking, and a table of findings in which no region, network, pattern or neuron is consistent for an emotion category. From these she concludes that categories such as fear are populations of variable instances, grouped by a goal and constructed by categorization with a concept. She rejects basic-emotion and causal appraisal theories as positing a "Lockean essence". This is the record's only read statement of the view. The record's philosophy holdings sharpen it. Pernu ([LIT-147](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-147.md)) shows that many-to-one realisation at a fine grain does not rule out one variable at a coarser grain, so degeneracy alone does not carry the conclusion, and Table 1 has to. Searle ([LIT-482](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-482.md)) shows that Barrett's comparison with money is to observer-relative function, not to institutions. Rivals the appraisal account, [THEORY-055](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-055.md). Proposed: one theoretical paper, no independent test, and the reply unread. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-058](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-058.md) v2 | Disorders are causal loops, not latent causes | Three traditions that do not cite one another for it put self-sustaining loops where a latent cause would be. Borsboom ([LIT-547](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-547.md)) makes disorder an alternative stable state of a strongly connected symptom network, kept up by hysteresis after its trigger has gone. Salkovskis, Sighvatsson and Sigurdsson ([LIT-538](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-538.md)) make it a threat meaning protected by the behaviour it drives. Kendler ([LIT-539](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-539.md)) finds causal loops across levels, from genes to culture. The convergence is real; the evidence is indirect, simulated or clinical, and none of it is an individual time series showing hysteresis, so the account is Proposed. It says nothing about what starts a disorder. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md) | Markov blankets exist around almost any set | The formal core of Bruineberg et al.'s critique ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md), C4 in [NOTE-447](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-447.md)). In a directed acyclic graph the blanket of a node set A is its parents, children and the children's other parents, and A is conditionally independent of everything outside A and its blanket. That holds for every A, so any set whose blanket leaves something outside gets a valid internal, blanket and external partition. Having a blanket therefore picks out no set. In Friston's soup ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) the set was picked by spectral clustering with k = 8, not by the blanket. Active because it is a short derivation that anyone can check. It covers graphical (Pearl) blankets and the 2013 procedure. It does not cover the later sparse-coupling definitions at nonequilibrium steady state, which the record has not read. | Active |
| [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) v3 | Blanket placement is fixed by prior modelling | Bruineberg et al. ([LIT-603](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-603.md)) and Raja et al. ([LIT-598](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-598.md)) argue, by different routes, that the Markov blanket of the free-energy literature is placed and not found. The formal core is [THEORY-066](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-066.md): the partition takes the internal set as input. This account adds what the critiques show about practice. In Friston's soup ([LIT-526](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-526.md)) the graph was built from one kind of coupling and steady state was assumed when the run stopped. In published applications the blanket sits wherever the model needs it: in the receptors of a brain, the membrane of a bacillus, the beam joining two pendulums. The formalism also gives the same description to a membrane the cell makes and a beam nobody's states make. So the blanket presupposes the boundary it is offered as the criterion of. Active since 2026-10-27, narrowed to the 2013 formulation and the applications held. The later steady-state definitions have not been read, and the unrestricted claim is THEORY-1097, Proposed. | Active |
| [THEORY-091](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-091.md) | Joint loss doesn't show a phenomenal function | Block (1995), [LIT-643](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-643.md), §6. Marcel, Flanagan, van Gulick and Schacter argue from the thirsty blindsight patient who does not reach for the water, and Searle from Penfield's petit mal automatisms, that a function of phenomenal consciousness is to let information guide action. In blindsight access is missing too, and in petit mal nothing shows experience is missing at all. "The fallacy is: an obvious function of the machinery of access-consciousness is illicitly transferred to phenomenal consciousness." That experience causes access, so that the function is experience's after all, is "a bold hypothesis, not a fallacy", and the deficit cannot decide it. Proposed: single-source, and the distinction it rests on is argued from conceivable cases. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-094](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-094.md) | Neither report nor no-report isolates the NCC | Block (2007), [LIT-646](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-646.md), framed the methodological puzzle: the neural basis of experience can be found only by deciding whether it includes the machinery of access, and the evidence comes through report. The no-report paradigm was the answer. Block (2019), [LIT-637](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-637.md), argues it has "a fatal flaw": subjects not asked to report still think about what they see, and that thought is aligned with the percept (the "bored monkey" problem). Eliminating report isolates the basis of experience "only if it eliminates post-perceptual cognitive processing" correlated with the percept. Brascamp et al.'s inconspicuous rivalry, whose switches subjects detected at chance, is the one such design Block offers. The method is specific to rivalry so far, and Block says there may be no general solution. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-125](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-125.md) | Group emotion is possible, though none is shown | Huebner (2010), [LIT-702](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-702.md): a genuinely collective emotion is a state of a group that "could not be exhaustively characterized in terms of intentional states of individuals in aggregation". Fear requires danger detection, redeployment of attention, system-wide preparatory change and their coordination into one state with indicative content and imperative force; a distributed system can integrate routines that way. Some individual emotions are non-conscious, so a group's need not be felt, and emotion kinds are functional ("like vodka"), so lacking homologous mechanisms does not exclude groups. The paper establishes a possibility, not an instance: its worked case, the USS Palau crew, turns out to be "collective detection of danger in the absence of a fear response", and the replacement, the 2008 McCain–Palin campaign, is offered as "intuitively plausible" pending anthropological data. Proposed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-133](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-133.md) v3 | Higher-level properties can be the real causes | List & Menzies (2009), [LIT-722](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-722.md). Take causes to be difference-makers. Then Kim's exclusion principle fails, and a revised one holds or fails system by system. Given that a higher-level property makes a difference to an effect, its realizer is not a cause exactly when some nearest situation without the realizer has the property realized otherwise and the effect present; the record re-derived this. The claim that higher-level relations are typically insensitive to their realizers is an observation about scientific practice, and Pernu disputes the paper's main example. Which systems meet the condition is [QUESTION-213](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-213.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-138](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-138.md) | Causation is dependence under intervention | Woodward, "Causation and Manipulability" (SEP, 2001; revised 2023), [LIT-713](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-713.md). A cause is what changes the effect under a surgical, exogenous intervention, defined relative to the effect by M1–M4. The account separates total from direct causes by combining interventions, and treats natural experiments as interventions. Active as the standard the record uses for what a causal claim asserts. This statement says nothing about invariance, proportionality or levels. | Active |
| [THEORY-141](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-141.md) v2 | Transitions need between-collective selection | Okasha (2022), [LIT-749](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-749.md), restating with Buss and Michod a principle of the major transitions: a new collective can be undone by defectors, and succeeds only if higher-level selection trumps lower-level selection, usually through policing or aligned interests. | [THEORY-146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md) v2 | Industry funding skews unbiased researchers | Holman & Bruner (2017), [LIT-744](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-744.md). In a Zollman bandit model with methodological diversity, productivity-weighted influence and turnover, industry funding of agents whose methods favour the drug lowers the chance of converging on the better action, though no agent's beliefs respond to funding. A merit-based independent funder worsens it; one ignoring industry-funded trials counters it. Held as what the model shows; whether real fields work this way is QUESTION-315. | Active |
| [THEORY-148](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-148.md) | Transient diversity lets groups learn | Zollman (2010), [LIT-735](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-735.md): in a bandit model with beta priors, sparse networks and extreme priors each maintain diversity of pursuit and each improve reliability, but combined they keep diversity alive so long that agents fail to converge. | [THEORY-151](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-151.md) v2 | Objectivity lies in community criticism | Longino's critical contextual empiricism, as she states it in the SEP ([LIT-725](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-725.md)). | [THEORY-295](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-295.md) v4 | Reproducibility need not track truth | Devezer, Nardin, Baumgaertner and Buzbas (2019), [LIT-988](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-988.md), read in full in [NOTE-792](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-792.md). In a Markov-chain and agent-based model where each step tests one proposed linear model against the consensus by AIC or SC, replication cannot change the transition matrix. A boundary-testing population reproduces almost perfectly while rarely holding the true model, and correlations between reproducibility and truth depend on the strategy mix. The consensus is memoryless, scientists hold no beliefs, and an equal strategy mix is shown only never to be the worst, not best. | Active |

It rests on a premise the paper declares "beyond the scope" and does not argue, that scientists are morally responsible for foreseeable consequences of error (p. 563). The direct/indirect line is drawn sharply in the conclusion but only sketched, and the reply that scientists could report uncertainty instead of accepting is not engaged. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-446](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-446.md) | Reciprocal causation unrolls into acyclic graphs | Baedke, Fábregas-Tejeda & Prieto (2021), [LIT-110](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-110.md), read in [NOTE-111](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-111.md). A conceptual and visual model, worked by example for each type of niche construction and for two multi-species cases. There is no formal semantics, no completeness result and no empirical test; formalization is deferred. It sets synchronic co-constitution aside rather than refuting it, and the claim that the boundary is an "epistemic necessity" is stronger than the argument, which shows only that the model can draw one usefully. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-451](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-451.md) | Singular causal claims need more than RCTs | Cartwright (2021), [LIT-213](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-213.md), read in [NOTE-161](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-161.md). The point that RCT results are not by the method evidence about another population (save under random sampling from it) is strong and standard. That no method or handful of methods can warrant a singular claim is argued from the diversity of facts a causal-process theory of change needs, with one illustrative case. That such theories yield reliable predictions is asserted, with no track record; the paper gives no method for weighing the evidence and little on transport. The critique of RCT rigour is internal to the author's own reconstruction of "rigour". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-453](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-453.md) | Physical objects can be mere relation-bearers | Esfeld & Lam (2008), [LIT-895](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-895.md), read in full in [NOTE-695](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-695.md). Moderate structural realism: relations require relata, but relata need no fundamental intrinsic properties, and objects and relations depend on each other with no priority. Its distinctive move is primitive numerical diversity, which it says gives no identity of any sort. The GR sections show interpretive fit, not entailment. Identity is equivocal between §1, where symmetric space-times need primitive diversity, and §2, where the metric "completely determines" structural identity; the one concrete construction cited works only without symmetries and breaks the general covariance the view rests on. The no-priority argument assumes three options are exhaustive. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-459](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-459.md) | Exact duality excludes ontological emergence | De Haro & Butterfield (2025), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md), §14.3, read in [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md). A formal argument from equinumerosity and surjectivity, strictly proven for finite sets, with an argument on physical grounds for the infinite case (fn. 57). Emergence here is novel reference in the domain of application, a semantic condition, not an information measure. AdS/CFT is the exception only to incompatibility with non-epistemic emergence, not to "not indicative": on a theoretically equivalent reading, its "emergent gravity" "cannot be understood as ontological emergence". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-463](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-463.md) | Dynamics alone can't give strict irreversibility | Frigg & Werndl (2023), [LIT-114](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-114.md), the SEP entry, read in [NOTE-103](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-103.md). The impossibility half rests on standard consequences of Liouville's theorem, time-reversal invariance and Poincaré recurrence. The classification half is the survey's: it is stated account by account, not argued as a general result. The entry is classical only, excludes the direction of time, and reports rather than settles the disputes about each repair. | Active |
| [THEORY-465](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-465.md) | Being reproduced does not entail reproducing | Bourrat (2025), [LIT-157](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-157.md), read in [NOTE-100](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-100.md). A definitional framework with no model or data. Both measures are recipes and neither is computed. The proxy for autonomy (conditional mutual information) measures resemblance given the environment, not the range of backgrounds the definition names, and the two recipes given for it differ. The overlap claim rests on a premise shown only for retroviruses, and the conclusion's "necessarily" outruns it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-469](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-469.md) | Evolutionary niche isn't Hutchinson's niche | Trappes (2021), [LIT-169](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-169.md), read in [NOTE-155](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-155.md). The non-identity follows from a conceptual argument the reading grades strong. The three kinds of case that populate the gap are weaker: habitat degradation rests on a projected persistence failure, commensalism on one field study after the author's first candidate failed, and non-limiting resources on a "possible example". The result is scoped to Odling-Smee, Laland & Feldman's 2003 niche concept and to the externalist reading of selection pressure. It does not say the two niches differ much; they "still coincide to a large extent". | Active |
| [THEORY-485](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-485.md) | Wave-function realism leaves physics closed | Poltorak (2026), [LIT-164](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-164.md), an unrefereed preprint read in full in [NOTE-112](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-112.md). "Every physical effect has a sufficient physical cause" has two tacit parameters, a domain and a completeness relation. With the domain set to spacetime the principle fails under wave-function realism; with it set to the ontology of a complete fundamental theory it survives. The move to a breach needs a premise that wave-function realists deny. The conclusions are modest and close to analytic once the terms are defined. The target is conceded to be a picture, not a published argument, and the dynamical-to-causal bridge is asserted, not argued. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-491](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-491.md) | Randomisation adds only selection-bias control | Worrall (2007), [LIT-175](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-175.md), read in [NOTE-126](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-126.md). The case against the unknown-confounders argument is conceptual: frequentist balance is a long-run claim about repeated divisions, and a trial divides once. It does not show that randomised designs are no more reliable in practice than matched ones, and the meta-research cited is mixed. The selection-bias argument is conceded as "cast-iron", so the account does not say randomisation is worthless. Haphazard allocation is asserted to serve as well, without discussing whether such rules are predictable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-528](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-528.md) | Embedded cognition explains extended cases | Rupert (2004), [LIT-422](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-422.md), read in [NOTE-343](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-343.md). The past-endorsement dilemma is strong: without it, directory assistance makes Otto believe every listed number; with it, the organism's endorsement is the final authority. The memory comparisons are moderate: the internal side is cited research, the external side is thought experiment, and no experiment on an external store is run or cited. The step from "different fine-grained kinds" to "no useful coarse kind" is a challenge plus conservatism. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-537](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-537.md) | Causal warrant comes from eliminating rivals | Reiss (2015), [LIT-118](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-118.md), read in [NOTE-197](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-197.md) from the 2015 Durham working paper; the refereed version was not read. A conceptual proposal with one historical illustration, the 1950s smoking and lung cancer controversy, which the author says is not a test. What counts as relevant, and when to stop probing, is handed to context, and the four grades of warrant are admitted to be arbitrary. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-541](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-541.md) | Hand-built representations give away the answer | Chalmers, French & Hofstadter (1992), [LIT-414](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-414.md), read in [NOTE-359](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-359.md) from the preprint, with Burns's review of Fluid Concepts (1995), [LIT-457](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-457.md), read in [NOTE-375](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-375.md). The BACON critique is strong; the SME critique moderate, with no alternative encoding run; the two arguments against a representation module informal. Burns turns the charges on Copycat: its Slipnet holds the domain's relevant relations, and the symbol-grounding objection to SME applies to it equally. Nothing is measured in either text. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-550](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-550.md) | Clustering is not epistemically superior | Søgaard (2024), [LIT-162](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-162.md), read in [NOTE-108](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-108.md). A rebuttal of two arguments for clustering's superiority, the No-Bias Argument and the Simplicity-Truth Argument, by toy counterexample and by the technical literature on overfitting in unsupervised learning (Hansen & Larsen 1996). The negative claims are firm. The paper's positive step, that supervised classification is "at least as" justified, is under-argued and is not part of this account. | Active |
| [THEORY-556](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-556.md) v2 | Algorithms evidence kinds but don't define them | Watson (2023), [LIT-187](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-187.md), read in full in [NOTE-172](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-172.md). Three pairs of theses, one per task: the epistemic one (EC, EA, EG) accepted, the ontological one (OC, OA, OG) rejected, each on the same computability ground. The rejection is a bare possibility argument with no example of an uncomputable kind, and the acceptance is hedged ("or something very much like them") so far that it is hard to falsify. The pragmatic, context-relative view of kinds is asserted, not defended. Self-supervised learning and foundation models are outside its scope. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-569](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-569.md) | Coherence explanatory power favours richer sets | Hartmann & Trpin (2026), [LIT-165](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-165.md), read in [NOTE-168](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-168.md), which recomputed all three numerical claims. One theorem (TLI for singleton explanans sets), one counterexample (OLI fails) and two parameterised existence examples (a distal cause for P(H1) < .7; a negatively interacting cause for P(H1) = P(H2) < .75). The escape from Roche & Sober is representational: a set is scored differently from the conjunction, and the two-place theorems still hold for conjunctions. No characterisation says when the richer set wins, and the paper's claim that the measure "accommodates key scientific judgments" is more than the body shows. | Active |
| [THEORY-572](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-572.md) | Replication can't delineate an unclear effect | Feest (2019), [LIT-161](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-161.md), read in [NOTE-196](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-196.md) from the PSA 2018 manuscript; the version of record was not read. An informal argument with one historical case, the Mozart effect, declared "typical" without further evidence. The claim that direct replication says "nothing" about systematic error is overstated: multi-lab replications vary some tacit lab-level factors. The conclusion is scoped by the author to effects not yet well conceptualised, and to internal validity; the title and abstract drop that hedge. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-586](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-586.md) | ψ-ontic states can still represent knowledge | Hance, Rarity & Ladyman (2021), [LIT-090](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-090.md), read in full in [NOTE-072](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-072.md). The formal ψ-ontic/ψ-epistemic split is contradictory by stipulation, while the informal "ontic" and "epistemic" are not exclusive. So PBR and the related theorems bound the geometry of µ_ψ, not the interpretation of ψ. The paper proves nothing; its positive criterion (Eq. 6) is predictive incompleteness, and its Appendix A makes claims the record's readings contradict. The defensible paraphrase of PBR is "not ψ-epistemic in the overlap sense, given preparation independence". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-591](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-591.md) | Cognition is contingently bound to the brain | Adams & Aizawa (2001), [LIT-438](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-438.md), read in [NOTE-368](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-368.md), restated against Clark in 2010, [LIT-455](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-455.md), read in [NOTE-380](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-380.md) from a draft. Both marks are assumed: the first on a claimed consensus, the second on how mature sciences individuate kinds. The authors grant the parity principle and that cognition could extend; the claim is that it does not. The "no science of tool use" half is offered as a bet. Rupert, the other critic, rejects the derived-content argument as question-begging. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-594](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-594.md) | Inequivalent representations needn't sink OSR | French (2010 draft; SHPMP 2012), [LIT-170](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-170.md), read in [NOTE-162](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-162.md) from the unpaginated preprint. Every technical step is imported (Wallace, Earman, Ruetsche, Halvorson & Müger, Baker); the paper's contribution is interpretive and informal. The DHR result that statistics and charge kinds follow from the algebra is strong physics; that it favours OSR is French's reading. The modal "trans-world" structure is proposed, not developed, and the combined third option "obviously requires further elaboration". | Proposed |
| [THEORY-600](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-600.md) | Justice alone can't define disease | Veit (2025), [LIT-098](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-098.md), read in [NOTE-097](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-097.md) from the PhilSci-Archive preprint. The target is Kukla's institutional definition: a condition is a health condition iff medicalising it would be best for collective wellbeing. The argument is informal and has two horns. One is a thought experiment (p. 14). The other rests on an asserted, undocumented premise about how medical tools evolve (p. 15). The extension from Kukla to "any purely normativist account" is asserted, not shown case by case. Veit concedes the first horn bites only without moral consensus. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-604](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-604.md) v2 | Most dualities are adjunctions to an opposite | Corfield (2017), [LIT-115](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-115.md), read in [NOTE-141](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-141.md). A short programmatic paper. That most dualities of interest are covered by constructions around adjunction is shown by worked exposition of standard cases, not proved. There is unlikely to be "a single monolithic account" (pp. 59–60). Reserving "duality" for structural reversal is a stated preference, and the verdicts on string dualities are a paragraph each. The proposal that philosophers of physics need homotopy type theory is an expectation. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-610](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-610.md) | Structure, not ontology, survives theory change | Worrall (1989), [LIT-315](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-315.md), read in [NOTE-297](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-297.md). Epistemic structural realism, credited to Poincaré, offered as the one position that keeps both the no-miracles argument and the pessimistic induction. The support is one worked case, which Worrall himself calls unrepresentative because the equations survive intact, and an appeal to the correspondence principle with one further example. "Structure" and "structural approximation" are undefined. The view is agnostic about what there is; the ontic turn, Ramsey sentences and the Newman objection belong to later work. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-612](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-612.md) | Niche construction can't cause selection itself | Hazelwood (2023), [LIT-156](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-156.md), read in full in [NOTE-137](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-137.md). A dilemma against strong reciprocal causation in the extended evolutionary synthesis, aimed at Laland and colleagues. Emergence is Wilson's synchronic dependence plus autonomy, cashed out as composition; causation is Woodward's interventionism with independent fixability. Its force rests on a process/product split for selection and a compositional reading of realization, both defended by citation and flagged as contestable, and its second horn considers only two non-emergent options. The weak sense, that organisms and environments affect each other, is granted as unobjectionable. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-627](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-627.md) | Learned nudges need cognitive inspection | Schmauder et al. (2023), [LIT-179](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-179.md), read in [NOTE-171](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-171.md). An argument by analogy from Hausman's reply to Friedman: a test drive is not enough if you must repair the car. Its evidence is reported from others: an RL agent moved choices of a target lottery from 50% to 70% by exploiting documented biases (Dezfouli et al. 2020), and AI advisers learned dishonest advice against simulated clients. No case of an undocumented bias is given; that is the paper's conjecture, and its oversight proposal is unspecified. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-631](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-631.md) | Unitary and open QT can't be ranked neutrally | Cuffaro & Hartmann (2021), [LIT-037](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-037.md), read in full in [NOTE-077](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-077.md). Stinespring dilation one way and dropping Lindblad terms the other make the two frameworks a tie on ontic dependence (OntFund-1) and on justification (EpFund-1). The verdict for the open theory comes from OntFund-2, which holds only if orthodox and Everettian readings are all that count, and from EpFund-2, which rests on imperfect preparation. Explanatory fundamentality is effectively abandoned. The paper proves nothing formal, and its "tout court" conclusion outruns §4. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-637](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-637.md) | Unlimited sharing can harm open science | Leonelli (2023), [LIT-189](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-189.md), read in [NOTE-098](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-098.md). An openly normative argument from four illustrative cases (GISAID, software stigma, crop-data linkage, the reproducibility debate) and the author's earlier qualitative work. That sharing-first open science can reduce diversity and worsen injustice is moderately supported; that this degrades reliability is argued, not measured. The positive proposal, openness as judicious connection, gives no decision rule, and the critique targets an ideal type the author admits many initiatives do not fit. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-639](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-639.md) | Inductive risk pervades the whole inquiry | Douglas (2000), [LIT-139](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-139.md), read in [NOTE-145](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-145.md). Three worked cases from one domain, dioxin toxicology and its regulation, on secondary data (EPA 1994; Kociba et al. 1978; Goodman & Sauer 1992). The structural point and the variation in slide scoring are strongly supported. The 100-fold figure is cited from Finkel (1988) and Greenlee et al. (1991). This is the descriptive half of the paper; the claim that values are therefore required is [THEORY-442](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-442.md). | Active |
| [THEORY-640](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-640.md) | Cross-modal representation convergence is weak | Huh, Cheung, Wang & Isola (2024), [LIT-302](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-302.md), read in [NOTE-286](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-286.md). Across 78 vision models, those solving more VTAB tasks agree more in mutual k-nearest-neighbour structure; language models with lower bits-per-byte agree more with vision models on 1,024 image–caption pairs. The cross-modal score "only reaches 0.16" of 1, is maximised over layer pairs, and the metric was chosen after CKA "revealed a very weak trend". It is local neighbourhood agreement that rises with competence, not kernel equality and not convergence to a model of reality. | Active |
| [THEORY-648](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-648.md) | Social facts constrain from outside | Durkheim (1894; book 1895), chapter I of Les Règles de la méthode sociologique, [LIT-484](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-484.md), read in French in [NOTE-391](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-391.md). A definition argued from examples, which its author calls "un simple résumé des données immédiates de l'observation" (n. 3). Its two load-bearing steps are asserted: that what is neither organic nor individual-psychic must have society as its substrate, and that constraint is present even where no one feels it. It is a claim about the object of sociology, not a group-mind thesis. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-657](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-657.md) | Emergence marks are independent of novelty | McKenzie (2025), [LIT-141](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-141.md), read in full in [NOTE-124](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-124.md). The book stipulates novelty as the definition and runs twelve further characteristics over about thirty cases. The Kondo effect is novel and continuous; the liquid–gas transition is discontinuous and adiabatically connected; BKT and the hexatic phase were predicted before they were found; Butterfield's cases are novel and reduced. [NOTE-124](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-124.md) says no THEORY follows from the book as a whole, since its definition is stipulated and the logical relations among the characteristics are left open by its own account (§24). This is the part of it that the counterexamples carry. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-658](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-658.md) | Teleology line depends on the account's purpose | Nahas & Sachs (2023), [LIT-192](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-192.md), read in [NOTE-094](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-094.md) from the accepted manuscript. A metatheoretical argument: naturalising teleology serves at least two relatively autonomous projects, advancing biology and settling the naturalism debate, with different success criteria. It is worked on one dispute, the demarcation from dissipative structures. The positive pluralism (Deacon for naturalism, Walsh and the organisational approach for biology) is only "tempting to suggest", and the boundary between the projects is never drawn. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-669](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-669.md) | Nomological ψ pays in the theory of laws | Chen (2018), [LIT-204](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-204.md) ([NOTE-175](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-175.md)), maps the realist readings and splits the nomological one into strong and weak. Belot (2011), [LIT-100](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-100.md) ([NOTE-110](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-110.md)), ranks the costs of ψ-as-law: time-indexed laws are the serious obstacle, grades of necessity tolerable. Allori (2021), [LIT-200](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-200.md) ([NOTE-154](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-154.md)), makes ψ an ingredient of the law, which may be time-dependent and non-unique, and so concedes Belot's point that ψ behaves like an initial condition. Each move is an informal argument. Chen reports, without endorsing, the objection that the weak reading is too cheap, and Allori's reply embraces the case it treats as a reductio. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-673](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-673.md) v2 | Price equation is a generalization-sketch | Luque (2016), [LIT-205](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-205.md), read in [NOTE-101](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-101.md) from the PhilSci manuscript. The derivation and the diallelic re-derivation are strong; the generalization-sketch reading is a moderate argument by analogy with f = ma plus two case studies, whose authors recovered results already derivable otherwise. The reply to "tautology" answers the word, not the critics' point, which Luque concedes in §7.2. The paper's prescription, that biologists should adopt the equation, is asserted without comparison. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-674](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-674.md) v2 | Causal-method share in economics rose to 31.7% | Garg & Fetzer (2024; arXiv v2 2026), [LIT-079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-079.md), read in full in [NOTE-083](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-083.md). GPT-4o-mini, nine passes per paper over the first 30 pages of 44,852 working papers, edges kept in at least 4 of 9 passes. The direction of the trend holds across overlap thresholds, its level does not (mean causal share 0.152 at EO = 1, 0.270 at EO = 9), and it nearly vanishes once method mix and graph volume are controlled. Validation covers paper-level method labels only, with RCT precision about 0.02. The association of causal structure with top-five publication rests on year-fixed-effect regressions over different subsamples and is not part of this claim. Promoted 2026-10-20 on the measurement alone (ADR-047 v3); the economics claim is held as THEORY-824. | Active |
| [THEORY-687](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-687.md) | Naive duals need metaphysics to pick a world | Le Bihan & Read (2018), [LIT-113](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-113.md), read in [NOTE-152](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-152.md) from the accepted manuscript. A nontechnical survey whose central argument is informal. It assumes a duality relates empirically equivalent models (weaker than De Haro & Butterfield's isomorphism of a bare theory), that each model is read naively and internally, and that structuralism is set aside. Its reading said it supports no existing THEORY directly; this files the conditional verdict the survey argues for, and nothing more. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-690](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-690.md) | Dualities give no real underdetermination | De Haro & Butterfield (2025), [LIT-199](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-199.md), read in [NOTE-178](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-178.md). A case-by-case argument over the book's examples, with a logico-semantic fallback (each dual entails the common core) for a hypothetical genuine case. The rich-core verdict is argued from exact cases (bosonization, electric–magnetic duality, T-duality) and does not reach AdS/CFT or M-theory, where structural-realist readings were proposed and the common core is "partial … ongoing work in physics!". The commitment holds only where an interpreted common core exists, which the authors say is not true in general. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-694](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-694.md) | Experience resists any functional explanation | Chalmers (1995), [LIT-406](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-406.md), read in full in [NOTE-336](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-336.md), with Nagel (1974), [LIT-096](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-096.md), read in [NOTE-089](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-089.md), for the subjective character it starts from. The test is whether "you have explained the function but not the phenomenon" is a conceptual mistake: it is for life and reportability, not for experience. The decisive premise, that any physical process could conceptually occur without experience, is asserted and deferred to a book the record holds unread. Nagel's conclusion is weaker than Chalmers's: physicalism not refuted but not yet understandable. Naturalistic dualism and the double-aspect theory of information are the proposals built on the gap, not part of it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-802](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-802.md) v3 | Causal abstractions are fixed only up to basis | The general reading that [THEORY-243](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-243.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the three-unit network it proves (batch 062). Wu et al. (2024), [LIT-961](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-961.md), conjecture that complex models have "multiple distinct fully correct abstractions" and that the causal-abstraction framework cannot settle structural equivalence; Makelov et al. (2023), [LIT-968](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-968.md), §8, grant that crossing component boundaries makes "illusory" tenuous, and answer by privileging components. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. Its only support is the constructed tie. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-814](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-814.md) | Reproducibility needn't indicate true consensus | The general reading that [THEORY-295](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-295.md) held before the promotion audit narrowed it to the memoryless consensus model it proves. Devezer, Nardin, Baumgaertner and Buzbas (2019), [LIT-988](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-988.md), read in [NOTE-792](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-792.md), present the decoupling of reproducibility from truth as a lesson for science, not only for their model. Their model has no beliefs, no learning and no memory in the consensus. Filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 so the wide form stays a thesis evidence can confirm or reject. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-824](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-824.md) | Design-based identification rose fourfold | Garg and Fetzer (2024; arXiv v2 2026), [LIT-079](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-079.md), read in full in [NOTE-083](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-083.md), read the rise in their extraction's design-backed share as a change in economics: "economic papers have increasingly incorporated causal inference methods to substantiate their claims over the past three decades". The record holds as shown, in [THEORY-674](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-674.md), only the extraction's series, whose edges were never checked against human labels and whose per-decade slope nearly vanishes with method-mix and graph-volume controls. This is the paper's reading, filed under [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4 when the narrowing dropped it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-855](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-855.md) v2 | Selective sharing misleads policymakers | Weatherall, O'Connor and Bruner (2020; arXiv 2018), [LIT-1341](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1341.md), read in [NOTE-1038](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1038.md). No result is fabricated and no scientist is biased; the audience is misled because it updates on a selected sample as if it were not selected. It is a property of a stylized model, which the authors call "how-potentially"; it does not show that any real audience was misled this way, nor that an audience aware of the selection would be. | Active |
| [THEORY-953](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-953.md) v3 | Converging quality-space models target experience | Isaac (2025), [LIT-1361](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1361.md), read in [NOTE-1163](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1163.md): why a third-personal science of quality spaces counts as a science of experience. Relations between experiences, unlike bare qualities, show up in behaviour, so they can be compared across subjects; and models from different behavioural routes that converge are taken to target what the routes share. The argument does not exclude a shared stimulus geometry or a shared decision process as the common factor, the convergence is partial by the paper's own account, and averaging over subjects makes the target an ideal observer, which the paper leaves as an open puzzle. | Active |
| [THEORY-1076](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1076.md) v2 | Bohr doesn't support agential realism | Faye & Jaksland (2021), [LIT-1672](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1672.md), read in [NOTE-1220](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1220.md), from Bohr's writings and the secondary literature. Active as exegesis: Bohr's own definitions of "phenomenon" (1938, 1949) and the convergence of realist and antirealist readings that Bohr never denied atomic objects. The dualisms half is interpretive and weaker. It does not say that Barad's view is false, only that it is not Bohr's. | Active |
| [THEORY-1078](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1078.md) v2 | Possibility needs no actual constructor | Deutsch & Marletto (2015), [LIT-1663](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1663.md), §§1–2 and footnote 1, read in [NOTE-1219](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1219.md). Active as a reading of the paper's definitions, which are explicit. It bears on A11's remark that constructor theory "could sharpen" what the record means by "a constraint being real", and it splits that notion. A possibility is a fact about the laws, which no particular thing realizes; a constructor is realized, approximate and deteriorating. It does not say that the framework's basic principle I is true, nor that a law of possibility is, or is not, a constraint realized by something ([CLAIM-477](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-477.md)). | Active |
| [THEORY-1083](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1083.md) v2 | Agential realism is applied once, not analogized | Jaksland (2024), [LIT-1673](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1673.md), read in [NOTE-1230](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1230.md), from Barad's own statements (2007, 24 and 85, with her dismissals of analogy at 2007, 6, 7, 18, 24, 70 and 88). Active as a reading of what Barad holds, which is well supported by her text as quoted. It does not say that the conception she holds is sound: that rests on agential realism being correct as quantum mechanics, which Faye and Jaksland dispute ([THEORY-1071](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1071.md)). It does say that a use of her concepts outside physics by structural comparison is a use she disowns. | Active |
| [THEORY-1086](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1086.md) v2 | Social theory's independence is contingent | Jaksland (2024), [LIT-1673](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1673.md), read in [NOTE-1230](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1230.md), reconstructing an argument Barad "only ever alludes to". It is a conditional and the author leaves its antecedent open: whether any ontological feature is all-or-nothing is "an open question". He finds individualism "immediately more agreeable" as approximable, and the dualisms the harder case. The contingency half is argued (a counterfactual on Planck's constant); the no-approximation half is a candidate list, not a demonstration. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1097](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1097.md) | No Markov blanket formulation individuates | The wider claim dropped when [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md) was narrowed to Friston's 2013 formulation and promoted on 2026-10-27 ([ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) v4: a narrowing's dropped claims go to Proposed entries). Both critiques argue the general form, and the record holds neither of the later formulations it would have to reach. Its promote_when is [THEORY-073](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-073.md)'s own, moved here unchanged. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1174](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1174.md) | Industry funding biases science with no corruption | The wide form [THEORY-146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md) held before the eleventh status review narrowed it, kept as a Proposed reading by the [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md) kind-1 sweep of 2026-10-30: the source asserts it, and [THEORY-146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md), Active, is its evidence. The old title's "counteracts this only if it discounts" is restated as "that discounts ... counteracts this": the paper compares two funder policies and asserts no necessity, a mis-statement left with [THEORY-146](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-146.md)'s note. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1204](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1204.md) | Convergent quality spaces best indicate experience | Isaac's "own considered view" (2025), [LIT-1361](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1361.md), §5, kept here when the twenty-second status review narrowed [THEORY-953](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-953.md) and promoted it as a report ([ADR-065](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-065.md); [ADR-047](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-047.md), kind 1). The argument does not rule out a shared stimulus geometry or a shared response process as the common factor, and the convergence is partial by the paper's own account. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1251](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1251.md) | Organization is posited a priori, not found | Mossio, Montévil and Longo (2016), [LIT-1888](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1888.md), §§1 and 4, read in [NOTE-1461](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1461.md); the definitions are Montévil and Mossio's ([LIT-582](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-582.md), [TERM-070](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-070.md)). The paper states the principle's status and scope and supports it by history and analogy; it derives nothing from it here. Proposed: what the principle buys is untested in this paper. It does not say that closure is observed in every organism, nor that only organisms realize it. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1260](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1260.md) | Extractable world models needn't be inside agents | Richens, Abel, Bellot and Everitt (2025), [LIT-1891](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1891.md), read in [NOTE-1469](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1469.md). The paper says its recovery map is "from the agent's policy rather than its activations", that this is "strictly weaker", and that it shows "a world model encoded in the agent's policy, not its specific use"; it contrasts itself with Savage, whose fit exists even for a random policy. That the result applies to Block's lookup table ([LIT-642](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-642.md)) is immediate from Def. 5, which constrains only the map. Active: the paper's own statements plus a one-line corollary. It does not say whether a compact implementation must have a separable predictive part. | Active |
| [THEORY-1281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1281.md) | Conversation-analytic focus limits ventriloquism | Wilhoit (2016), [LIT-1923](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1923.md), read in [NOTE-1487](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1487.md). | [THEORY-1287](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1287.md) | Mechanist experiments don't fix boundaries | Craver and Bechtel (2007), [LIT-1928](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1928.md), pp. 553–554, read in [NOTE-1491](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1491.md). The four kinds of interlevel experiment "share a form with Mill's methods" and are symmetrical. A lesion deficit is "only prima facie" evidence of componency, since a part "not interactively integrated" may be a background condition (n. 10). "Integrated" is never defined, and nothing in the four experiments tests where the system's edge is. That leaves the mechanism's boundary to be fixed some other way. | Active |
| [THEORY-1288](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1288.md) | Mutual manipulability is unsatisfiable | Baumgartner & Gebharter (2016), [LIT-1934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1934.md), pp. 10–13, 18–20, and Baumgartner & Casini (2017), [LIT-1939](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1939.md), pp. 6–11; restated by Baumgartner, Casini & Krickel (2020) as Systematic Fat-Handedness. Read in [NOTE-1493](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1493.md) and [NOTE-1490](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1490.md). Active as a conditional: valid on supervenience and non-causal constitution, and checked step by step. It does not say that constitution cannot be known, only that no finite set of manipulations of whole and part shows it; and it is about simultaneous whole–part dependence, not about a diachronic cause inside a system, which can be intervened on surgically. | Active |
| [THEORY-1289](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1289.md) v2 | Clamping a part tests its componenthood | Bechtel and Abrahamsen (2010), [LIT-1936](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1936.md), contribution C3 (p. 326), read in [NOTE-1492](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1492.md). Smolen et al. (2001) fixed the concentration of CLOCK in a reduced model of the Drosophila clock, and oscillation continued. They concluded that the positive CLOCK loop "was not critical". That is a part that belongs to the system and not to "the responsible mechanism for that particular phenomenon". The clamp is an ideal intervention, cheap in a model and hard in vivo. It is not a test of where the system's boundary lies. | Active |
| [THEORY-1290](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1290.md) v2 | Fit alone can't choose among dynamical models | Bechtel and Abrahamsen (2010), [LIT-1936](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1936.md), read in [NOTE-1492](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1492.md). Circadian models came after the clock's parts were found in the laboratory, and they explore those parts' dynamics. Cognitive models posit their parts. "Empirical evidence can rule out specific models, but usually cannot decide between competing architectures" (p. 332). It does not say de novo models are worthless: they make the same six kinds of contribution, at weaker standing. Nor does it say that anchoring makes a model right. | Active |
| [THEORY-1291](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1291.md) | Interlevel causes are mediated by constitution | Craver and Bechtel (2007), [LIT-1928](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1928.md), read in [NOTE-1491](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1491.md). Parts and wholes are not distinct events. So, given transmission, distinctness or asymmetry views of causation, they cannot be cause and effect, and the symmetry of interlevel experiments is explained by constitution. The six worked cases translate. The account says nothing about whether a feedback loop crossing the mechanism's boundary changes the analysis, and its generality is assumed. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-1293](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1293.md) | One intervention shows constituency, given levels | Baumgartner, Casini & Krickel (2020), [LIT-1924](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1924.md), §§3–4, read in [NOTE-1494](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1494.md). Active as a conditional: the eight-line reductio is valid on Universal Constitution, Simultaneity and transitivity of co-occurrence, and checked. It does not say such interventions exist in any real system, that the condition is necessary, or where the boundary lies; and its line between causation and constitution is simultaneity, which is sharp only at a fixed time resolution. | Active |
| [THEORY-1294](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1294.md) | Constitution is inferred only abductively | Baumgartner & Casini (2017), [LIT-1939](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1939.md), §§4–5, their No De-Coupling account, developing the fat-handedness criterion of Baumgartner & Gebharter (2016), [LIT-1934](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1934.md), pp. 20–22. Read in [NOTE-1490](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1490.md) and [NOTE-1493](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1493.md). Proposed: a definition offered with no operationalization and no case from practice, which the authors say themselves. | [THEORY-2002](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2002.md) | Structure learning's problem is generating models | From the reading of [LIT-2835](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2835.md) in [NOTE-2092](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2092.md). Neacsu, So, Rutar, da Costa, Adams and Friston (2026), Minds and Machines 36:33, DOI 10.1007/s11023-026-09787-8 (open access). A conceptual review. It surveys what "structure learning" means across developmental, cognitive and machine-learning work, then defines Structure Learning in active inference as offline Bayesian model selection by model evidence, by refitting or by Bayesian model reduction or expansion. It names the open problem as generating the hypothesis space, not choosing within it. It reports no results. Here because the exchange called it the most useful single paper for what the free-energy literature covers. It maps that literature fairly but leaves active, data-choosing structure learning to [LIT-2815](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2815.md). It agrees with [THEORY-564](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-564.md)'s framing that reduction, not expansion, is the open half. Read in its NOTE (skimmed in part). | Proposed |

Proposed until its promote_when is met. | Proposed |

| [THEORY-2274](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2274.md) | Situated knowledge can still be realist | Massimi's perspectival realism, read in [NOTE-2366](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2366.md) from her primer, a stand-in for the book [LIT-1228](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-1228.md). On [QUESTION-129](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-129.md) it offers a procedural constraint on admissible perspectives, no self-certification and comparison across communities, for knowledge claims; whether it carries to normative standards is the question's. The primer states the view and gives none of the book's arguments, so the account is held only as stated. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2281](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2281.md) | Satellite clock comparisons agree with fibre | Riedel et al.'s account, from a 26-day campaign over four European institutes: the frequency difference between two remote clocks, estimated over a satellite link by signal exchange between local masers, agrees between TWSTFT and GPS PPP ("compatible within a confidence level of 68 %", p. 11), and for LNE-SYRTE and PTB agrees with comparisons over optical fibre, one run simultaneously (pp. 12–13). The authors treat the two satellite techniques as "completely independent" and the comparison as a way to find systematic effects in either. For the record it is independent evidence for [CLAIM-510](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-510.md), that a measured correspondence can be checked against evidence the measurement did not produce. | Proposed |
| [THEORY-2292](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-2292.md) | Slaving principle alone is only descriptive | Schmietendorf (2026), [LIT-2231](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-2231.md), read in [NOTE-2394](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2394.md). A perspective, reporting positions (Stephan, Bedau, Bishop) more than arguing one; the author finds the debate leaning reductionist. It restates Haken's account of slaving in brief, standing in for the unavailable review only that far. Bears on [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md)'s wording of constraint and on [CLAIM-526](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-526.md), as notes only. Proposed until the reading of the debate is confirmed by another survey. | Proposed |
